[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Nancy Glasgow's birth about 1822 at Inishrush is a family estimate retained as uncertain. The identified marriage notice does not state her age or birthplace.

A notice in the ''Londonderry Standard'' reported that on 14 January 1842 the Rev. William Kennedy McKay married [[Kyle-3461|John Kyle]] of Tyanee and Nancy, the sixth daughter of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] of Inishrush, County Derry.<ref>''Londonderry Standard'', marriage notice, 14 January 1842, transcribed in “County Tyrone Ireland Marriage Notices 1840-42,” [https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriages-notices-1840-42/ public transcription].</ref> This directly establishes Nancy's father, spouse and marriage date. It does not name the marriage place, her mother, or any child.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3902]] is assessed at 95% (proved). The 1842 marriage notice calls Nancy, wife of John Kyle of Tyanee, sixth daughter of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush. The older Adam-3902, dead 1844, fits the established multi-child household; Adam-1622 is a real younger Inishrush alternative but fits a sixth-daughter family less well.

Whole selected father-profile proposition; maternity and upstream ancestry assessed separately.

Next useful test: Inspect the original 1842 notice and Adam’s family/probate for a Kyle daughter.

Source basis already held: [https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriages-notices-1840-42/ Londonderry Standard, marriage notice, 14 January 1842, transcribed in “County Tyrone Ireland Marriage Notices 1840-42,” public transcription (https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriages-notices-1840-42/).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


[[Unknown-760890|Rose]] is retained only as Nancy's uncertain mother because the marriage notice names Adam but not Nancy's mother.

McKay was minister of First Portglenone Presbyterian Church, but its surviving marriage register begins in 1845. The archival gap does not disprove the reported 1842 marriage and cannot supply a marriage place.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records'', First Portglenone Presbyterian D2594/1 and MIC1P/24, [https://www.proni.gov.uk/files/proni/2026-01/PRONI%20Guide%20to%20Church%20Records.pdf PDF].</ref>

No later woman named Nancy Kyle should be identified with this profile without a record giving a compatible husband, age or relationship.
